### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s).

**26** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 500bc9d5c59dc1755ab2bb0c4fc60fa2c8e447e2`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **31** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 500bc9d5c59dc1755ab2bb0c4fc60fa2c8e447e2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f97110cc9c92b22585104d51693e81a62e72fac5` — the merge of head `f381e8f4d0d2bf5648fba97661e1841f6f05ceb7` into base `500bc9d5c59dc1755ab2bb0c4fc60fa2c8e447e2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f97110cc9c92b22585104d51693e81a62e72fac5 && git checkout f97110cc9c92b22585104d51693e81a62e72fac5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 500bc9d5c59dc1755ab2bb0c4fc60fa2c8e447e2 f381e8f4d0d2bf5648fba97661e1841f6f05ceb7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 500bc9d5c59dc1755ab2bb0c4fc60fa2c8e447e2 && git merge --no-ff f381e8f4d0d2bf5648fba97661e1841f6f05ceb7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 500bc9d5c59dc1755ab2bb0c4fc60fa2c8e447e2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 500bc9d5c59dc1755ab2bb0c4fc60fa2c8e447e2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `f381e8f4d0d2bf5648fba97661e1841f6f05ceb7`
Local-runs: none

Rendered by the seat's subagent, adversarially, from the card (#26474, body and all nine comments), the PR (#26605 body, 16-file list, net diff against `main` at the merge base `1080f0745f`), and the head's check-runs read at 2026-10-27T10:06Z. Nothing was built, run or re-run. Declaration face: the committed tree touches no published schema and no governed path (no `packages/spec/**`, no `docs/adr/**`), so the review owed is the one the `Clause-②: yes` line alone owes.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept set of the wire door, `POST /api/v1/automation/:name/toggle` — unchanged. Right.** The diff on `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts` is one import and one call line (:3080, `toggleFlow(name, enabled, activationCaller(context))`). Read at head against base: the `manage_metadata` capability gate (`refuseUngrantedFlowWrite`, :2722), the ADR-0126 §5 activation write-authority gate (`refuseUngrantedFlowActivationWrite`, :2750), the #3899 strict-body checks and the #7535 `getFlow` 404 probe all sit ahead of the call at the same lines on both sides. No gate that was enforced before is skipped; the caller reaches the service only after both authority gates have judged it.

**Public surface of `@objectstack/service-automation` — widened. Right, and declared.** `FlowActivationStore` is re-exported from the package entry (`src/index.ts:35`); its `setActive(row)` becomes `setActive(row, options?: MetadataActivationWriteOptions)`. An optional parameter on an exported interface: a one-argument implementation still satisfies it (the new service test's recording store and the spec's own `TwoParameterService` pin prove the pattern). `AutomationEngine.toggleFlow(name, enabled, caller?)` implements the parameter the contract already declares (`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts:1018`, landed by #26545) and adds no surface of its own. `InMemoryFlowActivationStore` and `ObjectStoreFlowActivationStore` inherit core's `setActive(row, options?)` (#26551) and needed no edit.

**Public surface of `@objectstack/runtime` — unchanged. Right.** `activationCaller` is a new export of `domains/activation-gate.ts` only; `packages/runtime/src/index.ts` re-exports nothing from that module (its one wildcard is `export * from '@objectstack/core'`). Not reachable from the built entry.

**Actor provenance — from the engine's audit stamps, not a literal. Right.** No `created_by`, `updated_by`, `user_id` or `actor` is written anywhere in the diff. `flowActivationWriteOptions(caller)` builds `{ context: { isSystem: true, positions: [], permissions: [], userId } }`, which is core's own `SYSTEM_CTX` shape (`metadata-activation-store.ts:90`) plus the id, and satisfies `MetadataActivationWriteContext` (`{ readonly isSystem: true; readonly userId?: string } & Record...`). Core's `setActive` runs the keyed find, then the update or insert, under that context (:309-338), so the engine stamps the ledger row and the audit plugin records the same principal. The elevation is kept (`isSystem: true` in the type), and the write still runs grant-less (`positions: []`, `permissions: []`): the caller gains nothing from the channel. The brief's question is answered yes on both halves.

**Every in-repo `toggleFlow` caller — one, and it passes the caller. Right.** `git grep` at the head over `*.ts`/`*.tsx` outside `packages/spec` and outside tests finds exactly one call site, `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts:3080`. The other hits (`service-automation/src/plugin.ts:1143,1175`, `src/index.ts:168`, `src/flow-activation-store.ts:68`, `objectql/src/action-activation.ts:258`) are comments. `ui/`, `apps/`, `examples/`, `packages/client`: no hits. There is no internal caller without a user to judge.

**The channel carries the id and nothing else — pinned on both sides of the seam. Right.** Door side: `activationCaller` reads only `executionContext.userId` (string, non-empty) and returns `{ userId }` or `{}`; `automation-toggle-caller.test.ts` pins `toEqual({ userId: 'u_admin' })` against a context carrying positions, tenant and `isSystem: false`. Service side: `flowActivationWriteOptions` reads only `caller.userId`; `flow-toggle-caller-attribution.test.ts` pins that a JS caller smuggling `positions`/`permissions`/`tenantId` yields the bare system shape plus the id, and that `undefined`, `{}` and `{ userId: '' }` all yield `options === undefined` (an unattributed write, as before). The dogfood file adds the flow case (`showcase_scheduled_digest`, off then on, ledger row and audit row) to the same loop that pins the action and position doors; the dogfood matrix is skipped on PRs, so the 7/7 is the dev's local reading, consistent with the unit pins.

**The 18 exact-argument pins named in handoff `6436285999` — all 18 updated, and still live. Right.** 1 + 3 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 4 + 3 + 1 across the eight files named there, each now `expect.anything()` as the third argument. `expect.anything()` refuses `undefined`, and `activationCaller` always returns an object, so each pin still asserts a third argument is passed; the exact shape is pinned by the new door test. The stale prose the handoff listed is fixed in `engine.ts` (the ":5288-5294 no caller channel" docblock) and `flow-definitions.ts` (the "moved unedited" line). `flow-activation-store.ts:68` reads true at head as written and needed no edit.

**Divergence from the other two doors — by contract, noted.** The action and security doors (#26551) hand down the caller's whole execution context elevated (`activationWriteContext`), so their audit row's `tenant_id` can carry the caller's organization; the flow door hands down `userId` only, so its audit row's `tenant_id` stays null for an organization-scoped caller. That follows the contract's own narrowing (`Pick` of `AutomationContext` to `userId` alone, declared and reviewed in #26545) and the PR says so; under a walled posture only the platform operator, who has no organization, passes the §5 gate, so the observable gap is small. Not a defect of this PR; a reader who wants tenant attribution parity across the three doors files its own card.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/26474-flow-toggle-actor.md`: `@objectstack/service-automation: patch`, `@objectstack/runtime: patch`. Right. The two packages the diff moves are the two the changeset names; `@objectstack/core` is imported as a type only and unchanged; `@objectstack/dogfood` is `private: true` and owes none. Per the Post-Task Checklist ⑤ in AGENTS.md: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. No `!` in the title, no `(narrowing)` arm, no BREAKING banner owed. `Check Changeset` on the head: success.

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and in the changeset body, both line-initial and matching. Right. The claim (`6437525635`) pre-read `no` and delegated the measure to the dev on the diff; the dev measured `yes` because the published `FlowActivationStore.setActive` signature widens, the same measure #26551 applied to core's store. On the lane's own test (execution-duties: the public surface is what the built entry declaration reaches) the exported interface's new optional parameter is a widening, so `yes` is the accurate reading, and the spec lane rule adds that a `yes` declaration is never an error. The lane red line held: no `packages/spec/**` path in the file list. `Metadata-protocol: none` — right; nothing a metadata author writes changes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: `[]` in report `6438919887`. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag — "CI check runs on #26605 were not waited on." Read at 2026-10-27T10:06Z: 33 completed (22 success, 11 skipped: the UI lanes, Build Docs, Temporal, the Dogfood matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Build UI Deps, the two opt-ins), 0 failed, 11 still in progress: `Build Core`, `Test Core (1/8)` through `(8/8)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, and `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (the lane that runs `check-system-context-census`, which the dev reports exit 0 locally on this diff's new `isSystem: true` literal in `flow-definitions.ts`). Those eleven are the derived-gate families still to answer; this verdict is conditional on none of them turning red, which the seat reads before adoption.
- Dev flag — "the dogfood regression gate does not run on PRs or in the merge queue." Confirmed: the matrix is skipped on the head. The flow case's 7/7 is a local reading, backed by the two unit suites that pin each side of the seam.
- Dev flag — `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exit 3 then 0 after a full build. A prerequisite note, not a finding.
- `out_of_scope_findings`: the clone-as-`system` side note, carried by seat ruling `6434876664` item 3 (the `registerAndSaveFlow` / `PutOptions.actor` path), stays out of scope as ruled. The tenant-attribution divergence in ① is this review's own observation, not the dev's; carrier none, no card owed by this PR.
- Prose drift, non-blocking: the `ObjectStoreFlowActivationStore` docblock (`flow-activation-store.ts`, "All access uses a system context") is now imprecise, since a write made for a caller runs under that caller's elevated context. The next PR touching that file can reword it.
- Escalated: nothing.
